The loader repeats the same verification after materialization. A\nverification failure serves no view.\n\nThe materialized representation is an ephemeral in-memory view. It is never\naccepted by import or restore, and serving it does not create a saved view,\nevent, receipt, checkpoint generation, or any other workspace mutation.\n\n## Query\n\n`bead query --checkpoint PATH` accepts the existing R004 query document. It\nuses the same grammar, predicate validation, sort ordering, limit, and\nprojection semantics as a live query, evaluated against the historical issue\nrecords in the ephemeral view. Event identity is the pair\n`origin_store_uuid:origin_event_sequence`.\n\nFor each identity, a delta is one of:\n\n- `added`, with only `after`;\n- `removed`, with only `before`; or\n- `changed`, with both `before` and `after`.\n\nObjects are compared as parsed JSON values, so object member order and output\nformatting are not changes. An\n67\t/// invalid checkpoint configuration is different: the probe retains that\n68\t/// error so a read-only command can still run, but a semantic mutation cannot\n69\t/// succeed silently without publication. `probe` (not\n70\t/// `discover`) is deliberate: an uninitialized workspace is an error to\n71\t/// `discover`, and `init` and `doctor` must keep handling that state.\n72\tfn publication_probe(no_auto_flush: bool) -> Option<PublicationProbe> {\n73\t    if no_auto_flush {\n74\t        return None;\n75\t    }\n76\t\n77\t    let config = match store::WorkspaceConfig::probe() {\n78\t        Ok(store::WorkspaceState::Ready(config)) => config,\n79\t        _ => return None,\n80\t    };\n81\t\n82\t    let conn = open_checkpoint_connection(&config.database_path())?;\n83\t    let sequence_before = service::read_live_event_sequence(&conn)?;\n84\t\n85\t    let checkpoint_config = service::load_checkpoint_config(&config.root.join(\".beads\"));\n86\t    if checkpoint_config\n87\t        .as_ref()\n88\t        .is_ok_and(|config| !config.auto_flush_enabled())\n89\t    {\n90\t        return None;\n91\t    }\n92\t\n93\t    Some(PublicationProbe {\n94\t        config,\n95\t        checkpoint_config,\n96\t        sequence_before,\n97\t    })\n98\t}\n99\t\n100\t/// Open a connection for the chokepoint's sequence reads, through the same\n101\t/// pragma-configured opener the store uses, so a concurrent writer does not\n102\t/// silently disarm publication.\n103\tfn open_checkpoint_connection(db_path: &std::path::Path) -> Option<rusqlite::Connection> {\n104\t    store::open_configured_connection(db_path).ok()\n105\t}\n106\t\n107\t/// The single post-commit publication chokepoint (plan 6.2.1 items 1-4).\n108\t///\n109\t/// Runs only after `dispatch_command` returns `Ok` -- that is, strictly\n110\t/// after the command's own transaction committed, never inside it -- so a\n111\t/// publication failure propagates to the caller without touching committed\n112\t/// work. Which commands publish is not a per-call-site decision: the probe\n113\t/// snapshots the live event sequence before dispatch, and publication runs\n114\t/// only if this invocation advanced it. The live sequence is a sound\n115\t/// mutation signal because every mutating command must append an audit\n116\t/// event and every read-only command must not\n117\t/// (`tests/mutating_command_event_contract.rs` enforces both), so read-only\n118\t/// and no-op commands never publish, and a newly added mutating command\n119\t/// inherits publication with no wiring at all: its mandatory event is the\n120\t/// trigger.\n121\t///\n122\t/// Advancing the sequence is necessary but not sufficient: publication is\n123\t/// also skipped when the checkpoint's pointer already covers the live\n124\t/// sequence (item 3), so a no-op mutation publishes no generation and\n125\t/// creates no object, and a checkpoint another publisher already carried\n126\t/// to this sequence or beyond -- the state a lost publication race leaves\n127\t/// behind -- is treated as success, not something to publish over.\n128\t///\n129\t/// That coverage check runs twice: once as a lock-free fast path, once as\n130\t/// the authoritative decision under the checkpoint publication lock\n131\t/// (item 4), because a concurrent publisher may replace the pointer\n132\t/// between the two. The lock serializes publication -- object writes,\n133\t/// pointer replacement, tombstone application -- independently of the\n134\t/// SQLite write path, so a worker that loses the race waits for the\n135\t/// winner, rereads the pointer it published, sees a sequence at or beyond\n136\t/// its own, and returns success without publishing over it.\n137\t///\n138\t/// Item 5 lives at this function's edge: the command already returned\n139\t/// `Ok`, so every failure from the publication tail is a split outcome --\n140\t/// mutation committed, checkpoint did not advance -- and is reported as\n141\t/// [`Error::PostCommitPublicationFailed`] rather than whatever the\n142\t/// underlying error would have printed on its own. The disarm paths (no\n143\t/// connection, unreadable sequence, nothing to publish) stay silent\n144\t/// successes: they are decisions not to publish, not failures to. A malformed\n145\t/// checkpoint configuration is retained by the probe and reaches this\n146\t/// boundary only when the command advanced the event sequence, so it reports\n147\t/// the same post-commit split instead of failing open.\n148\tfn publish_after_commit(probe: &PublicationProbe) -> Result<()> {\n149\t    publish_committed_state(probe).map_err(|source| Error::PostCommitPublicationFailed { source })\n150\t}\n151\t\n152\t/// The fallible publication tail the chokepoint wraps: everything after\n153\t/// the decision to publish, whose failure can no longer touch the\n154\t/// committed mutation.\n155\tfn publish_committed_state(probe: &PublicationProbe) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n156\t    let Some(conn) = open_checkpoint_connection(&probe.config.database_path()) else {\n157\t        return Ok(());\n158\t    };\n159\t    let Some(sequence_after) = service::read_live_event_sequence(&conn) else {\n160\t        return Ok(());\n161\t    };\n162\t\n163\t    if sequence_after <= probe.sequence_before {\n164\t        // This invocation committed nothing the checkpoint carries; leave\n165\t        // any pre-existing dirtiness for `sync flush-only` to publish.\n166\t        return Ok(());\n167\t    }\n168\t\n169\t    let checkpoint_config = probe\n170\t        .checkpoint_config\n171\t        .as_ref()\n172\t        .map_err(|source| anyhow::anyhow!(source.to_string()))?;\n173\t\n174\t    let checkpoint_base = probe.config.root.join(\".beads\");\n175\t    if service::read_covered_event_sequence(&checkpoint_base)\n176\t        .is_some_and(|covered| covered >= sequence_after)\n177\t    {\n178\t        // The durable checkpoint already covers the live event sequence;\n179\t        // publishing again would mint a generation with nothing new to\n180\t        // carry (plan 6.2.1 item 3).\n181\t        return Ok(());\n182\t    }\n183\t\n184\t    // Serialize with every other publisher (plan 6.2.1 item 4). Past this\n185\t    // point the pointer stays stable until this publication finishes.\n186\t    let publication_lock =\n187\t        service::acquire_checkpoint_publication_lock(&checkpoint_base.join(\"checkpoint\"))?;\n188\t\n189\t    // The authoritative lost-race decision, under the lock: reread both\n190\t    // the live sequence and the pointer another publisher may have just\n191\t    // replaced. A pointer that now covers the live sequence covers this\n192\t    // invocation's own committed sequence too, so this worker's generation\n193\t    // has nothing to carry -- success, exit 0, nothing published over.\n194\t    if let Some(sequence_now) = service::read_live_event_sequence(&conn) {\n195\t        if service::read_covered_event_sequence(&checkpoint_base)\n196\t            .is_some_and(|covered| covered >= sequence_now)\n197\t        {\n198\t            return Ok(());\n199\t        }\n200\t    }\n201\t\n202\t    let mut store = store::SqliteStore::from_conn(conn);\n203\t    service::publish_forensic_checkpoint_holding(\n204\t        &publication_lock,\n205\t        &mut store,\n206\t        checkpoint_config,\n207\t        &checkpoint_base,\n208\t    )?;\n209\t\n210\t    // Silent on success (plan 6.2.1 item 6): no command's output gains a\n211\t    // field or a line. A failure propagates after the command's own output\n212\t    // has already been printed, so the committed mutation stays visible.\n213\t    Ok(())\n214\t}\n215\t\n216\t/// Publish a restore that had to initialize its target during this invocation.\n217\t/// Such a workspace did not exist when the normal pre-dispatch probe ran, so\n218\t/// it needs the same post-commit publication tail armed after activation. The\n219\t/// restore summary event makes the source pointer dirty, and this publication\n220\t/// carries that event plus the new provenance receipt into a fresh generation.\n221\tfn publish_newly_restored_state(no_auto_flush: bool) -> Result<()> {\n222\t    if no_auto_flush {\n223\t        return Ok(());\n224\t    }\n225\t    let config = match store::WorkspaceConfig::probe()? {\n226\t        store::WorkspaceState::Ready(config) => config,\n227\t        _ => return Ok(()),\n228\t    };\n229\t    let checkpoint_config =\n230\t        service::load_checkpoint_config(&config.root.join(\".beads\")).map_err(Error::Internal)?;\n231\t    if !checkpoint_config.auto_flush_enabled() {\n232\t        return Ok(());\n233\t    }\n234\t    let conn = store::open_configured_connection(&config.database_path())?;\n235\t    let live = service::read_live_event_sequence(&conn).unwrap_or(0);\n236\t    if service::read_covered_event_sequence(&config.root.join(\".beads\"))\n237\t        .is_some_and(|covered| covered >= live)\n238\t    {\n239\t        return Ok(());\n240\t    }\n241\t    let mut store = store::SqliteStore::from_conn(conn);\n242\t    service::publish_forensic_checkpoint(\n243\t        &mut store,\n244\t        &checkpoint_config,\n245\t        &config.root.join(\".beads\"),\n246\t    )\n247\t    .map(|_| ())\n248\t    .map_err(|source| Error::PostCommitPublicationFailed { source })\n249\t}\n250\t\n251\tfn execute_command(cli: Cli) -> Result<()> {\n252\t    // R030: publish the discovery override before anything resolves a\n253\t    // workspace, so `publication_probe` and every command's `discover` see\n254\t    // the same walk. Read before `cli` moves into dispatch.\n255\t    store::set_skip_foreign_workspaces(cli.skip_foreign_workspace);\n256\t\n257\t    // Arm post-commit publication before dispatch; a command that fails or\n258\t    // mutates nothing never reaches the publish step. The flag is read\n259\t    // before `cli` moves into dispatch.\n260\t    let no_auto_flush = cli.no_auto_flush;\n261\t    let restore_without_probe = matches!(&cli.command, SQLite cannot\n    // wait on a deferred read-to-write upgrade, even with busy_timeout set.\n    let tx = Transaction::new_unchecked(&conn, TransactionBehavior::Immediate)\n        .map_err(|e| Error::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to start transaction: {}\", e)))?;\n\n    // Parse scheduling policy\n    let policy = SchedulingPolicy::from_string(&opts.policy)?;\n\n    // Snapshot eligibility before the claim so the --why trace explains the\n    // decision as it was made (read-only; the claim below is the only\n    // mutation in this transaction)\n    let trace_factors = if opts.why {\n        Some(service::claim::collect_eligibility_factors(\n            &tx,\n            &opts.assignee,\n        )?)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    // Perform claim based on policy\n    let (enhanced_result, claim_result) = if matches!(policy, SchedulingPolicy::FifoV1) {\n        // Use existing FIFO claim for backward compatibility\n        let enhanced = service::claim_issue_with_lease(\n            &tx,\n            &opts.assignee,\n            opts.lease_ttl,\n            opts.renew_lease,\n            opts.fencing_token,\n            opts.single_claim,\n        )?;\n\n        let claim = ClaimResult {\n            bead_id: enhanced.bead_id.clone(),\n            assignee: enhanced.assignee.clone(),\n        };\n        (enhanced, claim)\n    } else {\n        // Use intelligent scheduling for R019 policies\n        let claim = service::claim_issue_with_policy(\n            &tx,\n            &opts.assignee,\n            &policy,\n            None, // model\n            None, // harness\n            None, // harness_version\n            opts.single_claim,\n        )?;\n\n        // Create enhanced result without lease for intelligent policies\n        let enhanced = service::EnhancedClaimResult {\n            bead_id: claim.bead_id.clone(),\n            assignee: claim.assignee.clone(),\n            lease: None, // Intelligent policies don't include lease info in basic result\n        };\n        (enhanced, claim)\n    };\n\n    // Build the decision trace if requested (backward compatibility with\n    // R001). Assembled from the pre-claim eligibility snapshot and the bead\n    // the claim actually selected — never from a second claim, which would\n    // silently assign an extra issue to the assignee (and defeat\n    // --single-claim), and never from post-claim state, which would describe\n    // the selected bead as in_progress/ineligible in its own trace.\n    let trace = trace_factors.map(|factors| {\n        service::claim::build_decision_trace(\n            factors,\n            enhanced_result.bead_id.as_deref(),\n            &opts.assignee,\n        )\n    });\n\n    // Commit transaction\n    tx.commit()\n        .map_err(|e| Error::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to commit transaction: {}\", e)))?;\n\n    // Output result\n    if opts.json {\n        let output = if let Some(trace_data) = trace {\n            // When --why is set, output enriched result with decision trace\n            serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::json!({\n                \"claim_result\": enhanced_result,\n                \"decision_trace\": trace_data\n            }))\n            .map_err(|e| {\n                Error::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                    \"Failed to serialize claim result with trace: {}\",\n                    e\n                ))\n            })?\n        } else {\n            // Standard claim result with lease information\n            serde_json::to_string(&enhanced_result).map_err(|e| {\n                Error::Internal(anyhow::anyhow!(\"Failed to serialize claim result: {}\", e))\n            })?\n        };\n        println!(\"{}\", output);\n    } else {\n        if let Some(bead_id) = &claim_result.bead_id {\n            println!(\"Claimed: {}\", bead_id);\n            println!(\"Assignee: {}\", claim_result.assignee);\n        } else {\n            println!(\"No eligible work found.\");\n        }\n\n        // Output decision trace in human-readable format if requested\n        if let Some(trace_data) = trace {\n            println!(\"\\n=== Decision Trace ===\");\n            println!(\"Version: {}\", trace_data.version);\n            println!(\"Policy: {}\", trace_data.policy);\n            println!(\"Assignee: {}\", trace_data.assignee);\n            println!(\n                \"Selection: {}\",\n                if trace_data.has_selection {\n                    \"Yes\"\n                } else {\n                    \"No\"\n                }\n            );\n\n            if let Some(selected_id) = &trace_data.selected_issue_id {\n                println!(\"Selected Issue: {}\", selected_id);\n            }\n\n            println!(\"\\nReasons:\");\n            for reason in &trace_data.reasons {\n                println!(\"  - {:?}\", reason);\n            }\n\n            println!(\"\\nEligibility Summary:\");\n            println!(\n                \"  Total Issues: {}\",\n                trace_data.eligibility_summary.total_issues\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"  Eligible: {}\",\n                trace_data.eligibility_summary.eligible_count\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"  Ineligible: {}\",\n                trace_data.eligibility_summary.ineligible_count\n            );\n\n            if !trace_data\n                .eligibility_summary\n                .ineligibility_reasons\n                .is_empty()\n            {\n                println!(\"  Ineligibility Reasons:\");\n                for (reason, count) in &trace_data.eligibility_summary.ineligibility_reasons {\n                    println!(\"    {}: {}\", reason, count);\n                }\n            }\n\n            if let Some(factors) = &trace_data.selected_factors {\n                println!(\"\\nSelected Issue Factors:\");\n                println!(\"  Priority: {}\", factors.priority);\n                println!(\"  Status: {}\", factors.base_status);\n                println!(\"  Assigned: {}\", factors.is_assigned);\n                println!(\"  Manually Blocked: {}\", factors.is_manually_blocked);\n                println!(\n                    \"  Unfinished Blockers: {}\",\n                    factors.unfinished_blocker_count\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn cmd_create(opts: cli::CreateOptions) -> Result<()> {\n    // Discover workspace\n report.covered_sequence.unwrap_or(report.live_sequence)\n            );\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let result =\n            service::publish_forensic_checkpoint(&mut store,
